messages:
laura: heads-up — we're proposing a new internal header for policy attribution: `X-RW-Policy: <policy-id>` to help console + billing map requests to routing policies. thoughts?
aj: curious — is this purely telemetry or also enforced routing?
miriam: telemetry only initially. goal is attribution for quota dashboards and cost centers. no enforcement in runtime.
sanjay: that reduces risk. do we need a separate header for cost-center (e.g., X-RW-Cost-Center) or put both in one blob?
derek: prefer separate headers: easier to index and less parsing in components. X-RW-Policy + X-RW-Cost.
laura: ok separate headers. big question: SDK compatibility. adding a required header would break proxies/clients. we should do opt-in via SDK flags.
aj: agree. plan: server accepts header if present; SDKs add it when opt-in flag set. need migration timeline.
miriam: console team wants to show policy-level tokens in the per-route dashboard ASAP. can we start with an edge proxy shim that injects header for dedicated/private customers?
sanjay: proxy shim is plausible for dedicated but not for hosted where customers call directly. SDKs must be the path for hosted.
derek: we can also do a safe fallback: if header missing, try to derive policy from API key -> fallback attribution in console with lower confidence. mark samples as inferred.
laura: good idea. UX-wise show a badge "inferred" vs "explicit". ops: how would telemetry look? sample rate?
miriam: keep sample rate same but add a boolean field in events indicating source=explicit|inferred. that way evals and regressions can filter.
aj: SDK implementation notes: python/ts/go should expose client option `policyHeader: {policyId, costCenter, optIn: true}`. default optIn=false. when true, SDK injects both headers. fallback mode logs a debug-level event.
derek: small code example for TS:
```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, policyHeader: { policyId: 'policy-123', costCenter: 'search-team', optIn: true } });
```
aj: tests: need end-to-end with console ingestion + quota attribution. also add integration test that ensures header is stripped when senders set `stripSensitiveHeaders=true` for on-prem customers.
sanjay: security note: headers could be faked. we should validate policyId server-side against known bindings for apiKey. if mismatch, mark as spoofed and ignore.
laura: agree. also add audit log entry when explicit header present and user is allowed.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: feature/telemetry/policy-header -> staging at 2025-06-12T10:00Z.
miriam: rollout plan proposal: week 1 — opt-in SDK release + proxy shim; week 2 — console dashboard flag to show explicit/inferred; week 4 — enable soft-mode server-side validation (mark spoofed but not block); week 8 — discuss hard enforcement for Dedicated customers only.
aj: can we add a short migration doc in devex? short checklist: (1) upgrade SDK, (2) set policyHeader optIn, (3) validate console view, (4) monitor inferred vs explicit ratio.
laura: yes I'll draft the checklist and tag @miriam for console screenshots.
sanjay: one more edge: offline SDKs that queue requests — ensure header persists across persisted tasks.
derek: noted. persistence will serialize headers with request envelope. make sure encryption for on-disk outlines.
laura: thanks everyone — next steps: aj and miriam to sketch SDK API, derek to spec server validation, me to write rollout checklist. ping here with PR links. :thumbsup:
